title: introduce-cudagraph-priming-buffer-and-compatibility-scoring-to-reduce-replay-warmup-regressions
author: Asha Patel
release_notes:
- Improve CUDA graph capture/replay stability by introducing a priming buffer and kernel compatibility scoring.
- Reduce warmup regressions for mixed sequence-length workloads.
- Fix KV-cache alignment bug that caused occasional token duplication under primed captures.
- No user-visible API changes; runtime internal behavior only.
description:
Motivation: Several production incidents and bench runs showed that CUDA graph capture/replay can regress tail latency and correctness for mixed-length traffic. Root causes we observed: (1) captures taken on a short, unrepresentative sequence can pick kernels and shape guards that later fail or trigger expensive fallbacks; (2) the kernel selection scoring ignores sparsity and dtype compatibility which leads to suboptimal kernel mappings during replay; (3) a subtle KV-cache offset alignment bug causes token duplication when a capture primes partial KV pages. This PR adds a lightweight priming buffer, a kernel compatibility scoring function used at capture-time, and a scheduler gate to avoid capturing until sufficient priming samples are collected. The PR also fixes the KV-cache alignment issue and wires telemetry for diagnosing capture health.

What this changes (high level):
- runtime/cudagraphs/priming_buffer.*: new priming buffer that conservatively stores short sequence samples per device and route. Buffer exposes an API to query representative shapes and average sparsity.
- runtime/kernels/compatibility_score.*: new scoring function that returns a compact compatibility score for (kernel, shape, dtype, sparsity). Scoring biases toward kernels with robust fallback semantics and lesser sensitivity to small sequence length drift.
- scheduler/capture_gate.*: capture gating logic that prevents starting a cudagraph capture until priming buffer reach a configurable threshold (defaults: 8 samples or 5s). Also supports force-capture CLI flag for debugging.
- runtime/kv_cache/align_fix.*: fix for KV cache offset calculation to ensure page alignment when reusing primed KV segments. Adds regression test that reproduces prior duplication.
- telemetry/capture_health.*: emits priming buffer hit/miss, capture_decision, chosen_kernel_score, and kv_alignment_events.
- tests/cudagraphs/*: unit and integration tests covering gating, scoring boundary cases, and an end-to-end replay correctness test under mixed-length traffic.

Design notes and rationale: The idea is to decouple capture priming from production traffic as little as possible while still collecting representative samples. The priming buffer is intentionally bounded and per-device to avoid OOM pressure. The compatibility score is a simple integer (0-100) computed from binary compatibility flags (dtype/sparsity/kernel-stability) and a small penalty for narrow shape margins. During capture we compute the score for potential kernel mappings and prefer the highest scoring mapping that meets a minimum threshold. If no mapping meets the threshold and gating is enabled, we delay capture until more priming data arrives; otherwise we fall back to the non-cuda-graph path. The scoring logic is kept deterministic and cached keyed by model+op so replay decisions are reproducible.

Review conversation (high level, chronological):
- Marcus Lee (review): "This looks promising — can you explain why we chose 8 samples as default? Also add a test that simulates high-sparsity kernel mismatch so we don't regress again."
- Author (Asha): "8 was chosen empirically from bench runs across 3 models (chat, code, summarization). Added comment and made it configurable via REDWOOD_CUDAGRAPH_PRIMING_SAMPLES. Added a high-sparsity test (compatibility_score_test covers this)."
- Elena Gomez (review): "Nit: telemetry key names should follow existing naming conventions (camelCase). Also we need to ensure privacy-safe content never enters priming buffer."
- Author: "Renamed keys to captureHealth.* and added redaction in priming buffer to strip token content; only shapes/sparsity stored. See priming_buffer_test for validation."
- Tomoya Saito (review): "KV alignment fix looks correct but please add a microbenchmark to show no perf regression for large KV reuse cases."
- Author: "Added microbench and included results in PR description; <1% throughput regression in worst case, often a win due to fewer fallbacks."
- Marcus (approve): "LGTM after CI green and one nit about log level for capture gating."
- Author: "Adjusted log level to debug for frequent events and info for state transitions."

CI & testing:
- CI initially failed on azure-gpu-integration: deterministic-seed test flaked (randomized scheduling produced a non-deterministic ordering). Reproducer added and fixed by seeding the scheduler's collector; rerun passed.
- GPU perf smoke job included microbench; results attached to CI artifacts.
- All unit tests and Linux GPU integration jobs passed on rerun. ci_status marked as pass.

Backward compatibility and rollout plan:
- Default gating enabled on main for a gradual rollout. We will monitor captureHealth metrics and only enable force-capture for select canaries.
- Console exposes a per-route override to tune priming sample threshold and minimum compatibility score.
- If customers see captures delayed too long, support can increase maxWaitMs or lower score threshold.

Potential follow-ups (tracked in ENG-1382):
- Adaptive thresholding: make sample counts depend on model variance detected at runtime.
- Persist priming buffer snapshots across restarts for hot routes.
- Backfill samplers for cold-start routes using synthetic sequences.

Merge details: squash-and-merge. Commit message includes a short summary and links to ENG-1382 and ENG-1399.

Notes for on-call / SRE: The captureHealth.telemetry stream will be the primary signal for regressions. Alert if captureDelay > 30s or captureFallbackRate > 5% for a route during a 5m window. The patch includes a dashboard tile in observability/ that teams can add to their service view.

QA checklist (completed): [x] unit tests added [x] integration tests for mixed-length replay [x] kv-cache regression reproduced and fixed [x] telemetry wired [x] perf microbench attached

If you want to exercise locally: export REDWOOD_CUDAGRAPH_PRIMING_SAMPLES=4 to lower the gating threshold and run tests/tests/integration/cudagraph_replay_mixed_lengths.py.

This PR is intentionally conservative: it prefers delaying capture over taking brittle captures, and adds fallbacks so we can iterate after collecting telemetry in prod.
mini_summary: Adds a priming buffer, kernel compatibility scoring, capture gating, KV-cache alignment fix, and telemetry to reduce cudagraph replay warmup regressions.
